title: Throughput and Quality Tradeoff Explorer — Quantized Batching (Nov 2025)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet explores concrete capacity tradeoffs when combining quantization and batching to meet regional throughput SLOs while bounding quality regressions. The goal is a quick, reproducible way to: (a) estimate GPU counts per region for a set of candidate quant+batch configs, (b) see expected quality delta on our internal eval slice, and (c) produce pragmatic recommendations (preferred config, canary checks, fallback).

Context / constraints: (why this exists)
- Hosted product is increasing traffic; procurement cycle pushes for predictable reserved capacity sizing for Dedicated and Private customers.
- We want to leverage quantization (NF4/INT8/INT4) and batching to reduce per-token cost while preserving evaluated quality on critical prompts.
- Target utilization window: target steady-state utilization = 70% (headroom for spikes / autoscale).
- Latency SLOs: chat p50 <= 300ms, p95 <= 800ms (these are conservative for sizing inputs).

Methodology / assumptions (simple, reproducible):
- Models considered: open-llama-7b (OL-7B), mpt-30b (MPT-30B).
- Hardware: A100-80GB, H100-80GB (on-region fleet mix for cost realism).
- Baseline single-GPU, batch=1, sequence len = 256 tokens. Measured tokens/sec approximations (empirical bench + historical):
  - OL-7B FP16: A100=1400 tok/s, H100=1900 tok/s
  - OL-7B NF4: A100=2000 tok/s, H100=2700 tok/s
  - OL-7B INT8: A100=2200 tok/s, H100=3000 tok/s
  - OL-7B INT4: A100=2600 tok/s, H100=3500 tok/s
  - MPT-30B FP16: A100=420 tok/s, H100=560 tok/s
  - MPT-30B NF4: A100=620 tok/s, H100=810 tok/s
  - MPT-30B INT8: A100=720 tok/s, H100=940 tok/s
  - MPT-30B INT4: A100=860 tok/s, H100=1100 tok/s
- Batching efficiency: real-world batching scales sublinearly. We use empirical batch efficiency multipliers (bench-derived): batch 4 -> x3.2, batch 8 -> x6.0 (A100) / x6.5 (H100), batch 16 -> x9.8 (A100) / x10.5 (H100). These represent tokens/sec at batchN = single_tok_s * multiplier.
- Quality: internal eval (representative production prompt set). Expressed as relative metric change vs FP16 baseline (higher is better). Values below are typical deltas observed on our eval harness (averaged over 4 tasks):
  - NF4: -0.5% relative metric change
  - INT8: -1.2%
  - INT4: -3.8% (must be validated on critical prompts)
- Latency impact: batching increases p50/p95 for individual requests (due to queueing). Example p50 at batch8: baseline p50_single * 1.9 (approx). Use these heuristics when recommending configs for low-latency routes.

Scenario matrix (quick reference): OL-7B on H100, comparison table (single GPU throughput -> effective GPU throughput at batch8):
  - FP16 single: 1900 tok/s -> batch8 eff = 1900 * 6.5 = 12,350 tok/s
  - NF4 single: 2700 -> batch8 eff = 2700 * 6.5 = 17,550 tok/s
  - INT8 single: 3000 -> batch8 eff = 3000 * 6.5 = 19,500 tok/s
  - INT4 single: 3500 -> batch8 eff = 3500 * 6.5 = 22,750 tok/s

Target regional throughput (tokens/sec steady-state) we used for this sheet:
  - us-west: 220,000 tok/s
  - us-east: 180,000 tok/s
  - eu-west: 140,000 tok/s
  - ap-southeast: 60,000 tok/s

Capacity calc method (example):
  Required GPUs = ceil( required_tokens / (per_gpu_eff_throughput * target_utilization) )
  where target_utilization = 0.70

Worked example: OL-7B, H100, INT8, batch8 for us-west:
  per_gpu_eff = 19,500 tok/s
  effective_at_util = 19,500 * 0.70 = 13,650 tok/s
  required_gpus = ceil(220,000 / 13,650) = ceil(16.12) = 17 GPUs
  Notes: expected eval quality delta = -1.2% (INT8). Latency: batching will increase p50; ensure route-level config allows batch8 or provide low-latency route with batch<=2.

Quick table: per-region recommended GPU counts (rounded, OL-7B focus) for three candidate configs: (H100, batch8, target_util=70%)
  - Config A: FP16 batch8 (no quant): per_gpu_eff=12,350 -> us-west: ceil(220k/(12,350*0.7))= ceil(25.5)=26 GPUs
  - Config B: NF4 batch8: per_gpu_eff=17,550 -> us-west: ceil(220k/(17,550*0.7))= ceil(17.95)=18 GPUs
  - Config C: INT8 batch8: per_gpu_eff=19,500 -> us-west: 17 GPUs (worked above)

Table summary (OL-7B, H100):
  Region  | FP16 b8 | NF4 b8 | INT8 b8 | Notes (quality delta)
  us-west | 26 GPUs | 18 GPUs | 17 GPUs  | NF4 -0.5%, INT8 -1.2%
  us-east | 21 GPUs | 15 GPUs | 13 GPUs  | scaled to 180k target
  eu-west | 17 GPUs | 11 GPUs | 10 GPUs  | prefer NF4 on eu-west due to cost
  apac    |  7 GPUs |  5 GPUs |  4 GPUs  | prefer burst/prefetch, smaller pool

Cost/quality tradeoff commentary (short):
- Jump from FP16 -> NF4: large throughput improvement (~+40%) with almost no observable quality delta on the eval slice (-0.5%). This is the sweet spot for many production routes.
- INT8 gives incremental throughput vs NF4 but adds moderately higher measurable metric regression (-1.2%). Good for bulk-embedding/async workloads where small quality drop is acceptable.
- INT4 is risky: large throughput gains but quality regressions are non-trivial (-3.8%) and can be prompt-dependent. Only use after per-prompt validation and graceful fallbacks.
- Batching: batch sizes 8–16 are the most cost-efficient throughput per GPU, but increase tail latency and make strict p50/p95 SLOs harder. For interactive chat routes prefer smaller batch targets (1–4) and use INT8/NF4 to recover throughput.

Mixed fleet recommendation (pragmatic):
- Default: OL-7B deployed as NF4 + batch8 on H100 in us-west/us-east for steady-state serving of non-low-latency routes. Rationale: good throughput boost; minimal quality delta.
- Low-latency routes (chat p50 sensitive): serve FP16 or NF4 with batch<=2 on a small pool of H100s (autoscale by QPS). Use request tagging to route critical requests to low-latency pool.
- EU-West: prefer A100 NF4 (cost/availability) if H100 spot capacity limited. Run capacity tests to confirm A100 multiplier assumptions.
- APAC: small dedicated pool (4–6 GPUs) + cross-region burst to us-west via smart routing for capacity peaks. Consider pre-warming KV cache for common prefixes to reduce per-request cost.

Validation checklist (must before ship of any aggressive quant config):
- [ ] Run per-prompt regression tests for a prioritized prompt set (must include safety and hallucination-sensitive prompts) — track relative metric and failure modes.
- [ ] Canary 2% traffic with quantized config + automatic rollback if metric delta > configured thresholds (e.g., >1.5%).
- [ ] Compare p95 latency and error rate under synthetic spikes (50% above baseline) for batch8 and batch16 configurations.
- [ ] Confirm tokenization/decoder path correctness for INT4 quantized weights on MPT-style models (sometimes requires kernel fallback).
- [ ] Update cost model sheet (finance) with per-region GPU price and expected monthly consumption delta.

Open questions / items to iterate:
- How does prefix-caching change effective required GPUs for each config? Short answer: caching can reduce steady tokens/sec by 10–40% depending on workload; we should run an SVT job to quantify for each customer class.
- What is the real-world variance between our bench multipliers and cloud provider instances (H100 vs custom-hardware)? Need a 48-hour soak test by region.
- Can we programmatically downgrade to FP16 for specific prompt classes when INT4 quality fails a lightweight predictor? Research task: cheap quality predictor for fallback decisions.

Immediate action items (next 2 weeks):
- Run regional soak tests (Aisha) for NF4/INT8 on H100 and A100 (72h) — collect tokens/sec, p50/p95, mem pressure, error rates. Jira: INFRA-3421.
- Implement canary gating in routing layer to allow 2% traffic to quantized pools (Miguel) — follow-up PR #789.
- Add per-prompt regression suite for INT4 (Li) and prioritize high-risk prompts.

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- This sheet intentionally optimistic on batch multiplier; real-world depends heavily on sequence length distribution and request arrival patterns. If arrival is bursty and burst coalescing is poor, effective batch multipliers drop and required GPUs increase closer to FP16 numbers.
- Saving on GPUs is only part of unit-cost story: consider backend I/O, cache hit amplification, and cross-region egress.

If you use this sheet: copy values into the monthly capacity planner and run sensitivity for +/-20% traffic and +/-10% multipliers.
